newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Retiring Joulwan says he knows when to bow out.
newsitem.headline: Retiring Joulwan says he knows when to bow out.

text.p: NATO's Supreme Allied Commander in Europe General George Joulwan, who is to retire next month, told Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn during talks on Tuesday he was a soldier who knew the right time to step down.

"I think a soldier has to know when it is time (to leave)," Joulwan said when asked by Horn why he was retiring. "I took the oath at (military academy) West Point in July 1957 - it's been 40 years and I've spent 22 of the last 36 years outside the United States - hopefully I've made a contribution."
Joulwan was meeting Horn during a stopover in Hungary on what he called a "farewell tour" of 20 capitals ahead of his retirement as NATO Supreme Allied Commander on July 10.

Earlier he received Hungary's highest honour that may be bestowed on a non-head of state, the Order of Merit Middle Cross with Star, in recognition of what Hungarian President Arpad Goncz described as "his assistance and valuable advice on the road to Hungary's full NATO membership."
Hungary is expected to be among the first group of countries to be invited to open talks on full NATO membership when the alliance holds its next summit in Madrid next month.
